chapters.title: The Official Ministry of Transportation (MTO) Driver’s Handbook

found.text: What drivers must do when they meet streetcars and school buses
Passing other vehicles
Passing vehicles, including bicycles, and driving in passing lanes
This is especially important if you are driving more slowly than other vehicles.
found.v: a driver SHOULD keep right WHEN the driver is driving more slowly than other vehicles

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.text: Pass these safety islands and zones at a reasonable speed.
found.v: a driver SHOULD pass a streetcar safety island OR zone at a reasonable speed

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.text: Always be ready, in case pedestrians make sudden or unexpected moves.
found.v: a driver SHOULD WATCH FOR pedestrians making sudden OR unexpected moves

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.text: Bicycles and mopeds travelling at a lower speed than other traffic are expected to ride about one metre from the curb or parked cars, or as close as practical to the right-hand edge of the road when there is no curb.
found.v: a cyclist SHOULD ride about 1 m from the curb OR parked cars, OR as close as practical to the right-hand edge of the road WHEN there is no curb, WHEN travelling at a lower speed than other traffic

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.text: Cyclists are not required to ride close to the right edge of the road when they are travelling at or faster than the normal speed of traffic at that time and place, or when they are turning left, or getting in position to turn left.
found.v: a cyclist MAY ride away from the right edge of the road WHEN travelling at OR faster than the normal speed of traffic at that time AND place OR WHEN turning left OR getting in position to turn left (EXCEPTION TO riding close to the right edge)

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.section: Sharing the road with large commercial vehicles
found.text: If a large vehicle in front of you is making a right turn, do not move up into the space that opens up in the right lane; you are putting yourself into a very dangerous position.
found.v: a driver SHOULD NOT move up into the space that opens up in the right lane WHEN a large vehicle in front is making a right turn BECAUSE this puts the driver in a very dangerous position

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.section: Sharing the road with large commercial vehicles
found.text: If you are in that lane, your vehicle will be squeezed between the trailer and the curb.

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.section: Sharing the road with large commercial vehicles
found.text: Stay well back until the truck has completely cleared the lane.
found.v: a driver SHOULD stay well back WHEN a truck ahead is making a right turn (… UNTIL the truck has completely cleared the lane)

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.section: Sharing the road with large commercial vehicles
found.text: Do not drive up into the left lane when a large vehicle is making a left turn in front of you.
found.v: a driver SHOULD NOT drive up into the left lane WHEN a large vehicle in front is making a left turn

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.section: Sharing the road with large commercial vehicles
found.text: Stay well back until the truck has cleared the left turn, or else you may get squeezed between the truck and the curb.
found.v: a driver SHOULD stay well back WHEN a truck ahead is turning left BECAUSE otherwise the driver may get squeezed between the truck AND the curb (… UNTIL the truck has cleared the left turn)

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.section: Sharing the road with school buses
found.text: When you see a school bus with its overhead amber lights flashing:
found.v: WHEN a driver sees a school bus with its overhead amber lights flashing: the listed rules apply

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.section: Sharing the road with school buses
found.text: These signals indicate that the bus is coming to a stop to pick up or drop off passengers

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.section: Sharing the road with school buses
found.text: Slow down and prepare to stop whether you are behind or approaching the bus
found.v: a driver SHOULD slow down AND be prepared to stop WHEN a school bus ahead OR approaching has its overhead amber lights flashing, whether the driver is behind OR approaching the bus

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.section: Sharing the road with school buses
found.text: If you are on a road with a median strip, only vehicles approach from the rear of the bus should prepare to stop
found.v: a driver SHOULD be prepared to stop for a school bus with flashing amber lights WHEN on a road with a median strip ONLY IF the driver is approaching from the rear of the bus (EXCEPTION TO preparing to stop whether behind or approaching)

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.section: Sharing the road with school buses
found.text: When you see a school bus with its overhead red lights flashing or its stop arm activated:
found.v: WHEN a driver sees a school bus with its overhead red lights flashing OR its stop arm activated: the listed rules apply

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.section: Sharing the road with school buses
found.text: You must stop whether you are behind or approaching the bus
found.v: a driver MUST stop WHEN a school bus has its overhead red lights flashing OR its stop arm activated, whether the driver is behind OR approaching the bus

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.section: Sharing the road with school buses
found.text: If you are on a roadway with a median strip, only vehicles approaching from the rear of the bus must stop
found.v: a driver MUST stop for a school bus with flashing red lights OR an activated stop arm WHEN on a roadway with a median strip ONLY IF the driver is approaching from the rear of the bus (EXCEPTION TO stopping whether behind or approaching)

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.section: Sharing the road with school buses
found.text: If you are approaching from the rear of the vehicle, stop at least 20 meters away
found.v: a driver SHOULD stop at least 20 m away from a school bus with flashing red lights OR an activated stop arm WHEN approaching it from the rear

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.section: Sharing the road with school buses
found.text: Do not proceed on your route until the bus moves, the overhead red lights have stopped flashing and its stop arm is no longer activated
found.v: a driver SHOULD NOT proceed UNLESS the bus has moved AND the overhead red lights have stopped flashing AND the stop arm is no longer activated

found.page_title: Sharing the road with other road users
found.section: Sharing the road with school buses
found.text: It is dangerous and illegal to fail to stop for a stopped school bus that has its overhead red lights flashing or its stop arm activated
found.v: a driver MUST stop WHEN a school bus is stopped AND has its overhead red lights flashing OR its stop arm activated BECAUSE failing to stop is dangerous

found.text: You must stop whenever you approach a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, regardless of whether you are behind the bus or approaching it from the front.
found.v: a driver MUST stop WHEN approaching a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, whether the driver is behind the bus OR approaching it from the front

found.text: When approaching the bus from the front, stop at a safe distance for children to get off the bus and cross the road in front of you.
found.v: a driver SHOULD stop at a safe distance WHEN approaching the school bus from the front BECAUSE children need room to get off the bus AND cross the road in front of the driver

found.text: If you are coming from behind the bus, stop at least 20 metres away.
found.v: a driver SHOULD stop at least 20 m away from the school bus WHEN coming from behind it

found.text: Do not go until the bus moves or the lights have stopped flashing.
found.v: a driver SHOULD NOT go UNLESS the bus has moved OR the lights have stopped flashing

found.text: If you are on a road with a median strip, only vehicles coming from behind the bus must stop.
found.v: a driver MUST stop for the school bus WHEN on a road with a median strip ONLY IF the driver is coming from behind the bus (EXCEPTION TO stopping whether behind or approaching)

found.text: You must obey the school bus law on any road, no matter how many lanes or what the speed limit.
found.v: a driver MUST obey the school bus law on any road, regardless of the number of lanes OR the speed limit

found.text: Be prepared to stop for a school bus at any time, not just within school hours.
found.v: a driver SHOULD be prepared to stop for a school bus at any time, not only within school hours

found.text: As well as the upper alternating red flashing lights, school buses use a stop sign arm on the driver’s side of the bus.
This arm, a standard stop sign with alternating flashing red lights at top and bottom, swings out after the upper alternating red lights begin to flash.
Remain stopped until the arm folds away and all lights stop flashing.
found.v: a driver SHOULD remain stopped WHEN a school bus has its stop arm out OR lights flashing (… UNTIL the arm folds away AND all lights stop flashing)

found.text: Note: It is illegal to fail to stop for a stopped school bus that has its red lights flashing.
found.v: a driver MUST stop WHEN a school bus is stopped AND has its red lights flashing

found.text: If you don't stop, you can be fined heavily and get six demerit points for a first offence.
found.v: a driver MUST stop for a stopped school bus with red lights flashing IF VIOLATED a heavy fine AND 6 demerit points for a first offence

found.text: If you are the vehicle’s registered owner, these fines, but not demerit points or jail time, may be applied to you.
found.v: IF VIOLATED (the owner's vehicle illegally passes a school bus) the registered owner may receive the fines but NOT demerit points OR jail time

found.text: If you are making a left turn behind one of these vehicles, do not pull up beside it to make your turn at the same time.
found.v: a driver SHOULD NOT pull up beside a motorcycle, bicycle, limited-speed motorcycle OR moped to turn at the same time WHEN the driver is making a left turn behind it

found.text: Stay behind and turn when the way is clear.
found.v: a driver SHOULD stay behind the smaller vehicle AND turn WHEN the way is clear

found.section: Dealing with particular situations at a roundabout > Pull over for emergency vehicles
found.text: If you have not entered the roundabout yet, pull over to the right if possible and wait until the emergency vehicle has passed.
found.v: a driver SHOULD pull over to the right WHEN an emergency vehicle approaches AND the driver has not yet entered the roundabout (… AND wait UNTIL the emergency vehicle has passed)

found.text: You may have to change lanes to overtake another vehicle, to avoid a parked vehicle or when the vehicle ahead slows to turn at an intersection.
Remember that spending a few seconds behind another vehicle is often safer than going around it.
found.v: a driver SHOULD spend a few seconds behind another vehicle instead of going around it BECAUSE this is often safer

found.text: The safety considerations and the sequence of steps to follow when changing lanes or passing
How to deal with specific situations when passing (for example, at night, streetcars)
If safe to do so, move over a lane to increase the space between your vehicle and the hazard.
found.v: a driver SHOULD move over a lane WHEN passing workers OR roadside vehicles ONLY IF it is safe BECAUSE this increases the space between the vehicle and the hazard

found.text: If your lane is blocked and no one is directing traffic, yield to the driver coming from the opposite direction.
found.v: a driver SHOULD let the driver coming from the opposite direction go first WHEN the driver's lane is blocked AND no one is directing traffic

found.text: When the way is clear, move slowly and carefully around the obstacle.
found.v: a driver SHOULD move slowly AND carefully around the obstacle WHEN the driver's lane is blocked AND the way is clear

found.text: Don't try to drive around the animal.
found.v: a driver SHOULD NOT try to drive around an animal WHEN the driver sees the animal on the road

found.section: Reacting to an approaching emergency vehicle
found.text: This will clear the intersection and minimize the possibility of a collision with the emergency vehicle should it be passing you on the side you intended to turn towards.

found.section: Reacting to an approaching emergency vehicle
found.text: When the emergency vehicle has passed, check to make sure the way is clear and signal before merging back into traffic.
found.v: TO rejoin traffic WHEN the emergency vehicle has passed: STEP 1 check that the way is clear; STEP 2 signal; STEP 3 merge back into traffic

found.section: Reacting to a stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck
found.text: When safe to do so, change lanes well in advance of an emergency vehicle or a stopped tow truck with its flashing amber lights.
found.v: TO slow down AND move over for a stopped emergency vehicle OR tow truck: STEP 5 change lanes well in advance of the emergency vehicle OR stopped tow truck with flashing amber lights ONLY IF it is safe

found.section: Reacting to a stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck > Failing to respond to an emergency vehicle
found.text: Please note the above law, fines and penalties are also applicable to a tow truck with its lamp producing intermittent flashes of amber light that is stopped on a highway.
found.v: a driver MUST obey the emergency-vehicle law above WHEN approaching a tow truck that is stopped on a highway with its amber lamp flashing IF VIOLATED the same fines AND penalties

found.section: Regulatory signs > Here are some common regulatory signs:
found.text: Slow traffic on multi-lane roads must keep right.
found.v: a driver MUST keep right WHEN the driver is driving slower than other traffic on a multi-lane road

found.section: Regulatory signs > Here are some common regulatory signs:
found.text: Stop for school bus when signals are flashing.

found.text: It informs drivers approaching from both directions that they must stop for a school bus when its signal lights are flashing.

found.text: Failing to stop for a school bus
found.v: a driver MUST stop for a school bus WHEN the law requires it IF VIOLATED six demerit points

found.text: Failing to share the road
found.v: a driver MUST share the road with other road users IF VIOLATED two demerit points

found.section: Left and right turns > If stopped > Space
found.text: When stopped behind another vehicle at an intersection, leave enough space to pull out and pass without having to back up.
found.v: a driver SHOULD leave enough space to pull out AND pass the vehicle ahead without backing up WHEN the driver is stopped behind another vehicle at an intersection

found.section: Left and right turns > If stopped > Space
found.text: Leaving this space protects you in three ways: it lets you pull around the vehicle in front if it stalls; it helps prevent you from being pushed into the vehicle ahead if you are hit from behind; and it reduces the risk of collision if the vehicle ahead rolls backward or backs up.

found.section: Left and right turns > If stopped > Wheels
found.text: At a large intersection with curved sidewalks where you are turning right, angle your vehicle to follow the curb so that no other vehi­cle can fit between you and the curb.
found.v: a driver SHOULD angle the vehicle to follow the curb WHEN the driver turns right at a large intersection with curved sidewalks BECAUSE then no other vehicle can fit between the vehicle and the curb

found.section: Left and right turns > Making the turn > Traffic check
found.text: If it is possible for another vehicle to overtake you while you are turning, check your blind spot before starting to turn.
found.v: a driver SHOULD check the blind spot WHEN the driver is about to start a turn AND another vehicle could overtake the driver during the turn

found.text: When stopped behind another vehicle at the intersection, leave enough space to pull out and pass without having to back up.
found.v: a driver SHOULD leave enough space to pull out AND pass the vehicle ahead without backing up WHEN the driver is stopped behind another vehicle at the intersection

found.text: Leaving this space protects you in three ways: it lets you pull around the vehicle in front if it stalls; it helps prevent you from being pushed into the ahead if you are hit from behind; and it reduces the risk of collision if the vehicle ahead rolls backward or backs up.
If your lane is blocked by a vehicle turning left or a vehicle edging into the intersection from the right, slow down or stop instead of pulling out to go around the vehicle.
found.v: a driver SHOULD slow down OR stop AND SHOULD NOT pull out to go around the vehicle WHEN the driver's lane is blocked by a vehicle turning left OR a vehicle edging into the intersection from the right

found.section: Roadside stop > The approach > Traffic check
found.text: If there is a chance of traffic or pedestrians overtaking you on the right, check your right blind spot just before pulling over.
found.v: a driver SHOULD check the right blind spot WHEN the driver is about to pull over AND traffic OR pedestrians could overtake the driver on the right

found.text: When you stop behind another vehicle, leave enough space to see its rear wheels or to pull around it without having to back up.
found.v: a driver SHOULD leave enough space to see the rear wheels of the vehicle ahead OR to pull around it without backing up WHEN the driver stops behind another vehicle
